# Queryable data: what Cognitive3D already captures

Design tracking plans with the end analysis in mind: know what Cognitive3D already captures (so you never re-instrument it) and how your custom instrumentation surfaces for querying afterward.

**If a Cognitive3D MCP server is connected, use it alongside this file — they answer different questions.** This file describes what the platform captures for every project, with units and planning implications. The MCP's `list_slicer_fields` and `get_field_values` tell you what a *specific* project actually holds, including its own custom properties and events. Reach for the MCP to confirm a field exists in the project you are working on; reach for this file to decide what is worth tracking in the first place.

## Captured automatically — do not re-instrument

The platform records 257+ session and event fields without any custom instrumentation. By planning category:

| Category | What's captured | Examples | Planning implication |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Session basics (27 fields) | Start time, duration, scene, session and participant identifiers, and which data streams are present. | `date` (Date); `duration` (Duration); `sceneId` (Scene) | Never track session length, scene visited, or "did gaze/events arrive" as custom events — all free. |
| App context (27 fields) | App name, version, engine, SDK version, editor-vs-build. | `c3d.app.version` (Version); `c3d.app.engine` (Engine); `c3d.app.inEditor` (In-Editor) — True for sessions run inside the Unity Editor rather than a built application. Useful for separating developer testing from real usage | Build/version comparisons need no custom properties. |
| Device & HMD (65 fields) | Headset and device model, OS, memory, battery, HMD orientation. | `c3d.device.hmd.type` (Headset); `c3d.device.os` (Operating System) | Device cohort comparisons are free — no custom device property needed. |
| Comfort, performance & movement metrics (75 fields) | Computed scores and aggregates — FPS, comfort, ergonomics, standing time, movement. | `c3d.metrics.fps_score` (FPS Score) — How consistently the app held the device's frame-rate target across the session; `c3d.metrics.comfort_score` (Ergonomics Score) — Physical comfort of the session, combining neck strain from head orientation with arm strain from controller reach; `c3d.metrics.average_fps` (Average FPS) — Plain average frame rate for the session, in Hz. Averaging this across sessions gives an average of averages, not a true fleet-wide frame rate | Do not instrument FPS, comfort, or posture yourself; recommend the built-in metrics. |
| Participant & user (25 fields) | Participant identity and participant properties (when the app sets them). | `c3d.participant.id` (Participant ID); `c3d.participant.name` (Participant Name) | Person-level cohorting works out of the box once participant ID is set. |
| Geography (9 fields) | Coarse location derived server-side (country, region). | `c3d.geo.country` (Location (Country)) | Geographic cohorting needs no instrumentation. |
| Multiplayer (15 fields) | Networking context and quality (when the multiplayer components are used). | `c3d.multiplayer.lobbyId` (Lobby ID) | Ping/room diagnostics come from the SDK components, not custom events. |
| Events & ExitPoll (8 fields) | Built-in lifecycle events (session start/end, scene change, idle) and ExitPoll answers. | `c3d.sessionStart` (Session Start); `c3d.SceneChange` (Scene Change); `cvr.exitpoll` (ExitPoll Instance) — Fired when an ExitPoll survey is presented to the user | Session lifecycle and survey responses are captured without custom events. |

## Automatic sensors

Sensors are continuous values recorded against the session timeline; per-session averages, minimums, and maximums are queryable. The Unity SDK records these automatically (hardware permitting):

- **Android Plugin**: Wifi Signal
- **App**: CPU Level, GPU Level, Passthrough, Power Saving Mode, Room Size (Playspace Boundary)
- **Battery**: HMD Battery Level, HMD Battery Status
- **Biometrics**: HP Cognitive Load, HP Cognitive Load Confidence *(HP Omnicept hardware only)*; HarmonEyes Attention Level, HarmonEyes Attention Score, HarmonEyes Fatigue Level, HarmonEyes Mental Readiness High %, HarmonEyes Mental Readiness Low %, HarmonEyes Mental Readiness Moderate %, HarmonEyes Mental Workload Level *(Requires HarmonEyes integration and supported eye tracking)*
- **Controller**: Left Controller Height From HMD (meters), Right Controller Height From HMD (meters)
- **Eye Tracking**: Left Pupil Diameter, Right Pupil Diameter *(HP Omnicept hardware only)*
- **FPS**: ASW, Average FPS (fps), Lowest 1% FPS (fps)
- **HMD**: HMD Pitch (degrees), HMD Yaw (degrees)
- **Heart Rate**: HP Heart Rate, HP Heart Rate Variability *(HP Omnicept hardware only)*
- **Multiplayer**: Multiplayer Ping, Multiplayer Ping Variance
- **Profiler**: Profiler Draw Calls, Profiler Main Thread Time (ms), Profiler Memory Used (MB)

## How your custom instrumentation surfaces

How YOUR instrumentation becomes queryable:

- **Custom event names** are filterable and groupable. Stable names are
  what make cross-session analysis possible — see the naming conventions
  in `data_strategy.md`. Variation belongs in properties, not names.
- **Event and session properties** are queryable by exact key and are
  typed (text / number / boolean). Send numbers as numbers: a
  `duration_seconds` sent as a string cannot be averaged or charted.
- **Participant properties** attach to the person, enabling cohort
  comparisons across sessions.
- **Custom sensors** record any continuous value against the session
  timeline; averages, minimums, and maximums become queryable per
  session.
- **Session tags** are applied by analysts on the dashboard — grouping
  that costs no code at all.

Planning rule of thumb: before adding any custom event, property, or sensor, check the tables above. If the platform already captures it, spend the instrumentation budget on app-specific context instead — that is the data only your app can provide.
